chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever prays outside of its proper time, his prayer is not valid."

key_terms.وَقْتٍ: Time (specifically the prescribed time for prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying outside of its designated time in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the chain of Abu Basir, this hadith articulates the principle of *adam al-istiqra'* (non-acceptance) for prayers offered outside their prescribed temporal boundaries. It underscores the Shia juristic view that time is an essential pillar (*rukn*) of obligatory prayers, distinguishing valid acts of worship from those lacking legal efficacy.
